Prevention: Removal and destruction of fully affected palms.
Rhinoceros beetle ( Oryctes rhinoceros ) can prevent the secondary infection of red palm weevil.
Maintain field sanitation and regular cleaning of crowns.
Adult beetles can be collected and killed
Monitoring: Monitoring the movement of adult beetles after the monsoon by installing light traps.
Oozing out of red brownish liquid from the entry hole of beetle.
Protruding out of chewed fibres in the bottom portion of palm.
In severe cases, wilting and bending of crown portion of palm is noticed.
Observing of gnawing sound of feeding grub during evening hours.
Direct Control: Place a mud pot attractant trap containing bits of tender stem, 2.5 litres of sugarcane molasses or pineapple pieces and 5 ml of vinegar or acetic acid at 5 traps per acre.
Replace the fluid once in the week to avoid mosquito breeding.
Restrictions: The control measures are ineffective if a wider tunnel is noticed in the trunk portion.
Non-systemic with stomach and contact action.
Sharply cut a fresh and live root slanting and feed the cut end with 10 ml of
Profenofos 50% EC along with 10 ml of water in a polythene bag.
Seal the bag with cotton thread.
Absorption should be checked within a day.
